quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The community choir is looking for new singers. Rehearsals are on Tuesday evenings from 7 to 9 p.m. at the town hall, and no experience is needed.
quests.question: No experience is needed to join the choir.
quests.hint: Read the last part of the second sentence.
quests.explanation: The notice says no experience is needed, so a first-time singer is welcome.
quests.evidenceLine: Rehearsals are on Tuesday evenings from 7 to 9 p.m. at the town hall, and no experience is needed.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: In the school laboratory, students must wear goggles at all times. Long hair should be tied back, and food or drinks are not allowed on the tables.
quests.question: Students must keep food and drinks off the laboratory tables.
quests.hint: Look at the rules about the tables.
quests.explanation: Food and drinks are not allowed on the tables, so eating there is not permitted.
quests.evidenceLine: Long hair should be tied back, and food or drinks are not allowed on the tables.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Marie lived in Paris until 1914, when she moved to London to work as a nurse. She returned to France after the war ended and opened a small clinic in her hometown.
quests.question: Marie opened her clinic before she worked as a nurse in London.
quests.hint: Put Marie's activities in the order they happened.
quests.explanation: She worked as a nurse in London first and opened her clinic only after returning.
quests.evidenceLine: Marie lived in Paris until 1914, when she moved to London to work as a nurse. She returned to France after the war ended and opened a small clinic in her hometown.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city will close Baker Street to cars next month. Only buses and bicycles will be allowed on the road, and the changes will start on the first of June.
quests.question: After the change, Baker Street will be open only to buses and bicycles.
quests.hint: Which vehicles will still be allowed?
quests.explanation: Only buses and bicycles will be allowed, so private cars will be kept out.
quests.evidenceLine: Only buses and bicycles will be allowed on the road, and the changes will start on the first of June.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Hi team, the meeting on Friday has been moved to 3 p.m. because the manager has a doctor's appointment in the morning. Please bring your reports and arrive on time.
quests.question: The meeting was moved because the reports are not ready.
quests.hint: Find the reason for the change.
quests.explanation: The meeting moved because of the manager's doctor's appointment, not the reports.
quests.evidenceLine: Hi team, the meeting on Friday has been moved to 3 p.m. because the manager has a doctor's appointment in the morning.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The new Zap phone has a battery that lasts three days and a screen that resists scratches. It costs $299, and buyers get a free case if they order before Sunday.
quests.question: The Zap phone costs less than $250.
quests.hint: Look at the price.
quests.explanation: The phone costs $299, which is more than $250.
quests.evidenceLine: It costs $299, and buyers get a free case if they order before Sunday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Octopuses are clever animals with soft bodies and eight arms. They have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, and the third sends it around the rest of the body.
quests.question: An octopus has fewer than three hearts.
quests.hint: Count the hearts mentioned.
quests.explanation: Two hearts serve the gills and a third serves the body, so an octopus has three.
quests.evidenceLine: They have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, and the third sends it around the rest of the body.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: To make lemonade, mix the juice of four lemons with one cup of sugar. Add four cups of cold water, stir well, and keep the drink in the refrigerator for an hour before serving.
quests.question: The lemonade rests in the refrigerator before it is served.
quests.hint: Follow the drink from the mixing to the serving.
quests.explanation: The recipe says to keep it in the refrigerator for an hour before serving.
quests.evidenceLine: Add four cups of cold water, stir well, and keep the drink in the refrigerator for an hour before serving.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Jae-won used to check his phone all evening. Now he puts it in a drawer at 8 p.m. and reads a book instead, which helps him sleep better.
quests.question: Jae-won still checks his phone throughout the evening.
quests.hint: Compare his old habit with his new one.
quests.explanation: He now puts the phone away at 8 p.m., so he no longer uses it all evening.
quests.evidenceLine: Now he puts it in a drawer at 8 p.m. and reads a book instead, which helps him sleep better.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Critics agree that the film starts slowly, but the second half is full of surprises. Most viewers loved the ending, though a few thought the whole movie was too long.
quests.question: Critics do not say that the film starts slowly.
quests.hint: Read what critics say about the beginning.
quests.explanation: Critics agree the film starts slowly, so they do say that.
quests.evidenceLine: Critics agree that the film starts slowly, but the second half is full of surprises.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Hi Dad, I put the keys under the flowerpot by the back door. The plumber will arrive at 2 p.m., so please make sure someone is home to let him into the kitchen.
quests.question: The plumber is due at 2 p.m.
quests.hint: Notice the time of the plumber's visit.
quests.explanation: The note gives 2 p.m. as the time the plumber will arrive.
quests.evidenceLine: The plumber will arrive at 2 p.m., so please make sure someone is home to let him into the kitchen.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Adults should sleep between seven and nine hours each night. People who sleep less than six hours often feel tired and find it hard to concentrate during the day.
quests.question: Sleeping only five hours a night can make it harder to concentrate.
quests.hint: Find what happens to people who sleep too little.
quests.explanation: Less than six hours often causes concentration problems, and five is less than six.
quests.evidenceLine: People who sleep less than six hours often feel tired and find it hard to concentrate during the day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The bank is offering a special account for students. There is no monthly fee, and students who save at least $20 each month receive a free notebook at the end of the year.
quests.question: A student who saves $30 a month qualifies for the free notebook.
quests.hint: Check the amount a student must save.
quests.explanation: The offer needs at least $20 a month, and $30 is more than $20.
quests.evidenceLine: There is no monthly fee, and students who save at least $20 each month receive a free notebook at the end of the year.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Renata runs for twenty minutes before work on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. On the other days she rests or stretches, because her doctor advised her not to run every day.
quests.question: Renata runs on five days each week.
quests.hint: Count the days she runs.
quests.explanation: She runs on three days a week, not five.
quests.evidenceLine: Renata runs for twenty minutes before work on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is. Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, so if the outdoor thermometer shows minus three, puddles will probably turn to ice.
quests.question: Puddles are likely to freeze when it is minus three degrees.
quests.hint: Compare the reading with the freezing point.
quests.explanation: Minus three is below zero, the freezing point, so puddles will probably freeze.
quests.evidenceLine: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius, so if the outdoor thermometer shows minus three, puddles will probably turn to ice.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Honeybees communicate by dancing. A bee that finds flowers returns to the hive and moves in a special pattern to show the other bees the direction and distance.
quests.question: The bees' dance shows the other bees how far away the flowers are but not which way to go.
quests.hint: Consider the two things the dance communicates.
quests.explanation: The dance shows both direction and distance, so it does help the bees know which way to go.
quests.evidenceLine: A bee that finds flowers returns to the hive and moves in a special pattern to show the other bees the direction and distance.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The school day starts at 8:15 a.m. and finishes at 3:00 p.m. There are five lessons, each fifty minutes long, and a lunch break of forty-five minutes.
quests.question: Students spend less than five hours a day in lessons.
quests.hint: Work out the total time spent in lessons.
quests.explanation: Five lessons of fifty minutes make 250 minutes, which is just over four hours.
quests.evidenceLine: There are five lessons, each fifty minutes long, and a lunch break of forty-five minutes.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: When crossing a road without traffic lights, stop at the curb and look right, left, and right again. Cross only when no vehicles are coming, and never run.
quests.question: Before crossing, you should look right, left, and right again.
quests.hint: Read the steps for looking before you cross.
quests.explanation: The passage says to look right, left, and then right again before crossing.
quests.evidenceLine: When crossing a road without traffic lights, stop at the curb and look right, left, and right again.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Notice: The central parking lot will be closed for repairs from Monday to Wednesday. Drivers can use the parking lot behind the station instead, which costs the same as usual.
quests.question: The central parking lot will be closed for a full week.
quests.hint: Count the days from Monday to Wednesday.
quests.explanation: Monday to Wednesday is three days, not a full week.
quests.evidenceLine: Notice: The central parking lot will be closed for repairs from Monday to Wednesday.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Luca is learning Portuguese with an app that gives him ten new words a day. After three months, he can read simple sentences but still finds it difficult to understand people who speak quickly.
quests.question: After three months, Luca can follow fast conversations easily.
quests.hint: Focus on the difficulty Luca still has.
quests.explanation: He still finds fast speakers difficult, so he cannot follow them easily.
quests.evidenceLine: After three months, he can read simple sentences but still finds it difficult to understand people who speak quickly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The lunch special at Luna's Kitchen includes a bowl of soup, a main dish, and a drink for $11. Dessert costs an extra $3.
quests.question: Adding dessert leaves the lunch special at $11.
quests.hint: Look at the price of dessert.
quests.explanation: Dessert costs an extra $3, so a lunch special with dessert costs $14.
quests.evidenceLine: The lunch special at Luna's Kitchen includes a bowl of soup, a main dish, and a drink for $11. Dessert costs an extra $3.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Noor is painting her bedroom pale blue this weekend. She moved the bed and the desk into the hallway yesterday, and she will bring them back on Sunday evening.
quests.question: Noor's furniture will be back in her bedroom by Sunday night.
quests.hint: Find when the furniture returns.
quests.explanation: She will bring the bed and desk back on Sunday evening, so they are in place by that night.
quests.evidenceLine: She moved the bed and the desk into the hallway yesterday, and she will bring them back on Sunday evening.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Teo's sister is getting married in July, and the whole family is helping with the wedding. Teo is in charge of the music, and his mother is making the cake.
quests.question: The music for the wedding is organized by Teo's mother.
quests.hint: Who is responsible for the music?
quests.explanation: Teo handles the music. His mother is making the cake.
quests.evidenceLine: Teo is in charge of the music, and his mother is making the cake.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city newspaper now has two editions: a printed one and an online one. The printed edition comes out only on weekends, while the online edition is updated every day.
quests.question: The online edition is published more often than the printed one.
quests.hint: Compare how often each edition comes out.
quests.explanation: The online edition is updated daily, but the printed one appears only at weekends.
quests.evidenceLine: The printed edition comes out only on weekends, while the online edition is updated every day.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The Eiffel Tower was built for a world fair in Paris in 1889. It was meant to stand for only twenty years, but it proved so useful for radio signals that it was allowed to stay.
quests.question: The Eiffel Tower stayed because it could be used for radio.
quests.hint: Find out why the tower was allowed to remain.
quests.explanation: It was useful for radio signals, which is why it was allowed to stay.
quests.evidenceLine: It was meant to stand for only twenty years, but it proved so useful for radio signals that it was allowed to stay.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air and give out oxygen. A large tree can give out enough oxygen for two people each day, which is one reason cities plant trees along their streets.
quests.question: Trees release carbon dioxide and absorb oxygen from the air.
quests.hint: Which gas do trees take in?
quests.explanation: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen, so the statement is reversed.
quests.evidenceLine: Trees take in carbon dioxide from the air and give out oxygen.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: At a traditional Korean party for a baby's first birthday, the child sits in front of several objects, such as a pencil, money, and thread. Families believe the object the baby picks first shows what the child's future may be like.
quests.question: The baby's family chooses the object for the child.
quests.hint: Who picks the object?
quests.explanation: The baby picks the object, not the family.
quests.evidenceLine: Families believe the object the baby picks first shows what the child's future may be like.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The night train from Leeds to Glasgow departs at 10:30 p.m. and arrives at 4:45 a.m. Passengers can book a bed, and blankets are provided free of charge.
quests.question: The night train journey takes about four hours.
quests.hint: Work out the time between departure and arrival.
quests.explanation: From 10:30 p.m. to 4:45 a.m. is over six hours, not four.
quests.evidenceLine: The night train from Leeds to Glasgow departs at 10:30 p.m. and arrives at 4:45 a.m.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: Young sunflower plants turn their heads to follow the sun across the sky each day. When the flowers are fully grown, they stop moving and stay facing east, where the morning sun warms them first.
quests.question: Fully grown sunflowers stay in one position.
quests.hint: Read what the mature flowers do.
quests.explanation: Once fully grown, sunflowers stop moving and keep facing east.
quests.evidenceLine: When the flowers are fully grown, they stop moving and stay facing east, where the morning sun warms them first.

quests.instruction: Read the passage carefully and decide if the statement is true or false.
quests.passage: The city marathon is 42 kilometers long, and this year more than five thousand people took part. Amit ran the first half in one hour and forty minutes, but he needed two hours for the second half.
quests.question: Amit ran the second half more slowly than the first half.
quests.hint: Compare the two halves of his race.
quests.explanation: The first half took 1 hour 40 minutes and the second took two hours, so it was slower.
quests.evidenceLine: Amit ran the first half in one hour and forty minutes, but he needed two hours for the second half.
